subject: TEST-FORMATTED-DATETIME function
notes: CLOSED by kb/Work PB255. Citation re-derived: cite.py --check 15.92.4 'the value returned is the ordinal character position at which the first error in argument-2 was detected' -> OK, rule 1. The per-digit range NARROWING and the zero arm were already right and are undisturbed; the three residues are all closed. (1) THE OFFSET SUBFIELD BOUNDS WERE JUSTIFIED BY THE WRONG CLAUSE. Fld.OffHour and Fld.OffMinute share their switch arms with Fld.Hour and Fld.Minute and were the only bounds in the table with no citation, while the adjudication defended them from 15.3.3.3 - which governs the COMMON TIME format by its own words ('the minutes subfield of the data (corresponding to mm in a common time format)'). The clause that governs them is 15.3.3.6.2: cite.py --check 15.3.3.6.2 'The offset-hours subfield of the data associated with a basic or extended offset time format shall contain a value from 00 to 23 inclusive' -> OK and the offset-minutes twin -> OK. The values coincide, which is exactly how a shared arm carried an unverified justification; both clauses are now named at the arm and the bounds are MEASURED by 2014/pb255_test_formatted_datetime_bounds OFFH=009 (offset-hours '25' - the interval [20,29] straddles 23 at the first digit and [25,25] exceeds it at the second, so 9) and OFFM=010 (offset-minutes '60' - [60,69] already exceeds 59 at the first digit, so 10), with OFF0=000 as the admitting leg so closing the bound cannot over-reject. (2) THE SHORT-ARGUMENT-2 ANSWER IS NOW WRITTEN DOWN. 15.92.3 places no size rule on argument-2 and the compiler applies none, so the shape is reachable and 15.92.4 is silent on it; docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3 D-TFD1 records the answer LENGTH(argument-2) + 1 on two grounds - the rule says the position AT WHICH the error was DETECTED (15.93.4 r1 b) says 'the position of the first character in error' when it means that), and 15.93.4 r1 c) is the standard's own convention for an argument that is valid but INCOMPLETE, '(FUNCTION LENGTH (argument-1) + 1)' (--check -> OK), cited as a convention the standard already chose for this shape and never as the governing rule for this function. SHRT=008 measures it. (3) THE NOTE'S LOWERCASE FORMAT is recorded as D-TFD2: 15.3.1.2 is normative about case ('four uppercase Y characters', --check -> OK) and a NOTE is not, so the NOTE's own program does not compile here and every fixture spells the format in uppercase - a substitution that was being made silently.
